notes.text: Will raise up — Will produce and send into the world in due time. A prophet like unto me - Christ was truly, and in all commendable parts like him, in being both a prophet and a king and a priest and mediator, in the excellency of his ministry and work, in the glory of his miracles, in his familiar and intimate converse with God.
I will require it — I will punish him severely for it. The sad effect of this threatning the Jews have felt for above sixteen hundred years together.

glossa.text: *A prophet of.* Although it may be taken historically of the prophets who after Moses were filled with the Spirit of God among the people of Israel, yet it is better taken of the Lord of the prophets, of whom the crowds filled by him said: *This is of a truth the prophet that is to come into the world ((Joan. VI))*. And elsewhere: *A great prophet is risen up among us ((Luc. VII))*.

notes.text: Sought — Diligently meditated upon.
Work — Either all his works, or that eminent branch of those works, his providence towards his people. Righteousness - His justice or faithfulness in performing his word.
Remembered — By their own nature, and the lasting benefits flowing from them, which are such as cannot easily be forgotten.
Meat — All necessary provisions for their being and well-being.

The works — All that he doth on the behalf of his people, or against their enemies. Truth - Are exactly agreeable to his promises, and to justice. Commandments - His laws given to the Israelites, especially the moral law. Sure - Constant and unchangeable.
Done — Constituted or ordered.

Redemption — The deliverance out of Egypt, which was a type of that higher redemption by Christ. Commanded - Appointed, or established firmly by his power and authority. For ever - Through all successive generations of his people to the end of the world. Reverend - Terrible to his enemies, venerable in his peoples eyes, and holy in all his dealings with all men.

The fear — True religion. Beginning - Is the only foundation of, and introduction to, true wisdom. This also is an alphabetical psalm. We have here the character and blessedness of the righteous, ver. 1-9. The iniquity of the wicked, ver. 10.

glossa.text: *I will give praise.* ((AUG.)) Here there is no confession of sins, but of praise: the one mourns, this rejoices: the one shows the wound to the physician, this gives thanks for health. *In the council.* Not rashly, but out of reason, namely for things eternal, as all the just do. ((CASS.)) *In the council of the just.* Here never among all the just, where the wicked are mingled with them, but they are seen already to sing in the fellowship to come, caught up by hope to the things above. *In the council,* which is, when they judge with the Lord. *In the congregation,* when they are gathered together out of the whole.

*Great works.* This is the matter and the cause of the confession. Great are the works of the Lord, in that he makes a godly man out of an ungodly. *Sought out.* ((AUG., CASS.)) To which nothing is like, while he suffers the devil to rage, etc., *as far as* not: *for his justice remaineth for ever and ever. Unto all the wills.* ((AUG.)) Nothing surpasses the will of God, who, even if he wills that thou sin not, yet does not prevent it. If he wills to spare the penitent, he wills also to punish the impenitent; so concerning man God always fulfils his own will, because man does nothing out of which God does not work what he wills.

*Confession and magnificence is his work.* ((CASS.)) As it were: I will give praise, because great are the works of the Lord. Any works soever are also great, if in them there be seen the intention and the will, which is the *confession* of sins, and the *magnificence* of good works: and *justice,* that is, the reward which is justly given.

*He hath made a remembrance.* ((ID.)) Secondly he says that the faithful are filled with a plentiful gift, promising the coming of the Lord, that the inheritance may be eagerly sought. ((AUG.)) *He hath made a remembrance of his wonderful works.* Humbling this man and exalting that, etc., *as far as* what shall he receive, he is glorified *glorificatur*; read *glorificatus*, "glorified", in the things to come?

*He hath given food.* ((CASS.)) He makes confession and magnificence, etc., *as far as* that all things may be fulfilled. *He will be mindful,* etc. ((AUG.)) Nor did he give the whole who gave a pledge, etc., *as far as* they enter through the piercing straits of the passion.

*The power of the works.* ((CASS.)) The power of the works is that the blind see, etc. Which things he made known to the Christian people. *That he may give them the inheritance,* this was the intent of the miracles, that they might believe.

*That he may give them the inheritance of the Gentiles.* ((ID.)) As it were: although he gives them the inheritance, yet they shall suffer many things. *The works of his hands.* ((ID.)) That is, of his power. *Truth,* while he restores to the converted what was promised: *Judgment,* which he threatens to the ungodly. ((AUG.)) *Truth,* which the holy martyrs hold, and for which they are also judged here; *and judgment,* whereby in time to come they shall judge those by whom they are here judged. ((ID.)) *The works of his hands are truth and judgment.* Let *truth* be held by those who are judged, etc., *as far as* this is the inheritance of the New Testament.

*All the commandments are faithful.* ((CASS.)) Because they keep those who keep them, they are not lies. *Confirmed.* Not sent forth in vain, as human words are: *Made,* not only spoken, *in truth,* because all are fulfilled.

*In equity.* ((AUG.)) Because all things are done with the balance of justice.

*He hath sent redemption.* ((CASS.)) Thirdly he affirms the redeemed, and the New Testament consecrated by eternal grace; or. *His name: the beginning of wisdom.* ((ID.)) That is, the Son, who in his humanity is *holy,* in the power of the Godhead *terrible.* Let the advocate therefore be loved, let the judge be feared, lest thou be negligent, lest thou despair.

The fear of the Lord. ((ID.)) The dread of judgment is the gate of conversion, if the discernment of love be added to it. *His praise continueth.* The intent of the psalm, whence Alleluia is prefixed, began with praise and ends in praise: the faithful people, delivered from the devil and giving thanks, has expressed what is to be done here also by the devout, and to be accomplished in heaven: here because he delivers, there because he crowns.

notes.text: Now concerning the next question you proposed. All of us have knowledge — A gentle reproof of their self-conceit. Knowledge without love always puffeth up. Love alone edifies - Builds us up in holiness.
If any man think he knoweth any thing — Aright, unless so far he is taught by God. He knoweth nothing yet as he ought to know - Seeing there is no true knowledge without divine love.
He is known — That is, approved, by him. Psalm i, 6.
We know that an idol is nothing — A mere nominal god, having no divinity, virtue, or power.
For though there be that are called gods — By the heathens both celestial, (as they style them,) terrestrial, and infernal deities.

Yet to us — Christians. There is but one God - This is exclusive, not of the One Lord, as if he were an inferior deity; but only of the idols to which the One God is opposed. From whom are all things - By creation, providence, and grace. And we for him - The end of all we are, have, and do. And one Lord - Equally the object of divine worship. By whom are all things - Created, sustained, and governed. And we by him - Have access to the Father, and all spiritual blessings.

Some eat, with consciousness of the idol — That is, fancying it is something, and that it makes the meat unlawful to be eaten. And their conscience, being weak - Not rightly informed. Is defiled - contracts guilt by doing it.
But meat commendeth us not to God — Neither by eating, nor by refraining from it. Eating and not eating are in themselves things merely indifferent.

For if any one see thee who hast knowledge — Whom he believes to have more knowledge than himself, and who really hast this knowledge, that an idol is nothing-sitting down to an entertainment in an idol temple. The heathens frequently made entertainments in their temples, on what hath been sacrificed to their idols. Will not the conscience of him that is weak - Scrupulous. Be encouraged - By thy example. To eat - Though with a doubting conscience.

And through thy knowledge shall the weak brother perish, for whom Christ died? — And for whom thou wilt not lose a meal's meat, so far from dying for him! We see, Christ died even for them that perish.
Ye sin against Christ — Whose members they are.
If meat — Of any kind. Who will follow this example? What preacher or private Christian will abstain from any thing lawful in itself, when it offends a weak brother?

glossa.text:
*Concerning these things.* As if he should say: You know as well as I that it is lawful to eat them; because we all have knowledge. This he says of those who, having knowledge, ate with offence. These he first reproves, and says that they do not know sufficiently. But others in ignorance ate under veneration of the idol.

*Knowledge puffeth up.* Of itself knowledge is unprofitable, with charity it is profitable. Of itself it puffs up into pride, like the demons, who by a Greek name are so called from knowledge. For the repressing of the elation of knowledge a sting was given to Paul. It is better to know our own weakness than the natures of things; he who adds this knowledge adds the sorrow of pilgrimage out of longing for the fatherland.
*But if any man love God.* He loves God who for charity's sake tempers his knowledge, that it may profit the brother for whom Christ died.

*Concerning meats.* Having found fault with their knowledge, he at length discloses what that true knowledge is. *An idol is nothing in the world.* That is, among the creatures of the world. For God formed the matter, but the folly of men gave the form. For whatsoever things are in creatures were made through the Word. But the form of a man in an idol was not made through the Word, as neither was sin made through the Word. But it is nothing, and men become nothing when they sin. *But one.* This he says, lest God be thought to be in the idol.

*For indeed there are many gods.* That is, many to the Gentiles: whom our God terrifies, that is, the demons, who, wishing to be seen as gods, exact for themselves the things that are owed to the true God, altars, sacrifices, and the rest. But ours makes men gods.

*God.* In three ways is God said. Substantively God is said, the Trinity. By adoption, the saints who by the grace of adoption are gods. By appellation, the demons and idols. *Of whom.* All things are from the Father, but created through the Son. Nor are some things through the Son and others through the Father, but the same: otherwise now not all things are through the Father, nor all things through the Son; but if all things are through the Father, then all things also through the Son; therefore the same things were made through the Father which were made also through the Son; the Son therefore is equal to the Father, and the operation of both is inseparable. *And one.* Of Christ, in respect of his humanity, he adds it, but of the Holy Spirit it was not needful.
*Is defiled.* Namely, through those who have the knowledge of one God, but not with charity, through whom the weak were led into this error, whose food is not defiled, but their conscience.
*Against Christ.* To sin against Christ is to deny Christ.

notes.text: Luke iv, 31.

A loud noise — For he was forbidden to speak. Christ would neither suffer those evil spirits to speak in opposition, nor yet in favour of him. He needed not their testimony, nor would encourage it, lest any should infer that he acted in concert with them.

glossa.text: *For he was,* etc. ((BEDA.)) The scribes said the things that were written in Moses and the prophets; Jesus, as God and Lord, freely added to the law of Moses himself, or changed, the things that were wanting; whence in Matthew: *You have heard that it was said to them of old,* etc. *But I say to you.*

*What have we,* etc. ((ID.)) This is not a confession of the will, but an extortion of necessity: as a runaway servant fears his master when he sees him, and entreats concerning stripes. For the demons, beholding the Lord upon earth, believed that they were straightway to be judged.

*Hold thy peace. ((ID.))* In fitting order the serpent's tongue, which first scattered venom, is first stopped, that it scatter no more, then, etc., *as far as* that the order of restoration in the Lord may be the same as that of perdition in the first-formed man.

*Tearing him. ((ID.))* Or shaking him, as certain codices have it. But Luke says that it hurt him nothing. Yet what Mark says, *tearing,* is the same as Luke's: *when he had cast him into the midst.* But as to what he added, *and hurt him not:* it is to be understood that that tossing did not weaken him: as demons go out with some limbs cut off or torn away.

((ID.)) The man delivered from the demon we understand to be the mind cleansed from unclean thought. But the woman consequently healed of her fevers, the flesh bridled from the fervour of concupiscence by the precepts of continence.

*What thing is this?* By the things which they see they are stirred up to the search of the things which they had heard. For to this end the Lord himself both works signs and gave to his disciples to work them, that by this the Gospel may be the more surely believed, while they who promise heavenly things to earthly men work heavenly and divine works upon earth.

registers.label: Spare
lines: They were astounded at his teaching.
He taught them as one with authority.
Even the unclean spirits obey his word.
What is this? A new teaching, and with authority!
The God of wisdom raises up a prophet to speak.
We will listen to the One God sends.
Come, let us worship the Word that commands.
Your word has authority, Lord. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: In the synagogue at Capernaum he opened the scroll and taught, and the room went still, for here was a voice like no scribe's.
A new teaching — and it has authority!
A tormented man cried out, and Jesus did not argue or explain; he spoke one word, and the unclean spirit had to go.
A new teaching — and it has authority!
The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom; great are his works, studied by all who delight in them.
A new teaching — and it has authority!
So we come to listen to the One whose word still heals and still commands. Speak, Lord.
A new teaching — and it has authority! Amen.
